title: Left component of a merged gate array
statement: Let $g_1 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1 \to \alpha$ and $g_2 : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_2 \to \alpha$ be two gate arrays, and let $g_1 \ast g_2 : \mathrm{Fin}\,(m_1+m_2) \to \alpha$ denote their merge, which agrees with $g_1$ on the indices $0,\dots,m_1-1$ and with $g_2$ on the indices $m_1,\dots,m_1+m_2-1$. Then for every $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1$, evaluating the merge at the index $i$ regarded as an element of $\mathrm{Fin}\,(m_1+m_2)$ (i.e. the same value $i < m_1$) returns $g_1\,i$.
hypotheses_covered: gate arrays g₁ over Fin m₁ and g₂ over Fin m₂
index viewed in Fin (m₁+m₂) via the left inclusion
replaced:
For every $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,m_1$, evaluating the merged array at the left-embedded index
$\mathrm{castAdd}\,m_2\,i$ recovers $g_1\,i$, i.e.
$\mathrm{mergeGates}\,g_1\,g_2\,(\mathrm{castAdd}\,m_2\,i) = g_1\,i$.
